title: The Command-and-Control Strategy: Avoid the Snares of Groupthink
coreMove: Give mission, context, and dissent channels instead of over-specifying method when the team is competent enough to adapt.
sourcePressure: Groupthink is structural: the cost of speaking up is visible, the cost of silence is hidden, and hierarchy makes silence look safe.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Replace leadership with vague autonomy or consensus with no command.

sourceAnchors.name: Auftragstaktik
sourceAnchors.detail: the source identifies the German mission-driven command tradition: tell subordinates the purpose, not the method.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Auftragstaktik gives the room a cleaner test: can people act from intent when the steps stop fitting the facts?

hook: Do not open with a battlefield metaphor for The Command-and-Control Strategy: Avoid the Snares of Groupthink.
Do not start by saying strategy is not about violence.
counterintuition: Avoid the reusable correction frame that the move is not X but Y.
Avoid a bland paradox about strength looking like weakness.
tryThisNow: No generic timer, pause, breathe, or list-three-options prompt.
No reusable ask what matters most prompt.
examples: No generic founder in a pitch deck unless the domain requires it.
No battlefield reenactment or invented historical anecdote.
